Settings.Title: Settings
Settings.Worklist.Enabled: Offer the worklist when entering patient details
Settings.Worklist.CallingAeOverride: Calling AE Title for the worklist
Settings.Worklist.CallingAeOverride.Capt: Leave empty to use this workstation’s own AE Title, which is what most sites want. Set it only when the worklist server expects a different name from the archive.
Settings.Worklist.Modality.Caption: Leave empty to list every modality, which is usually right for a department converting documents. Enter a value such as OT to narrow it.
Settings.Worklist.Range.AnyDate: Any date (can be slow on a busy worklist)
Settings.Worklist.ScheduledStation.Capti: Leave blank to match every station, which is usually right: the document is filed from a desk, not from the scheduled device.
Settings.Worklist.ExplicitDates.Caption: These two dates are used only when the interval above is set to an explicit range. Either may be left empty, in which case today is used for that end.
Settings.Worklist.MaximumResults.Caption: A guard against a mistyped search returning an entire schedule. The list says so when it has been cut short.
Settings.Worklist.AcceptAnyCertificate.C: Convenient on a closed network with a self signed certificate, and a hole anywhere else: it stops the worklist server being authenticated at all.
Worklist.Title: Modality Worklist
Worklist.Subtitle: Choose the scheduled procedure this document belongs to. The patient details are taken from it, so nothing has to be typed.
Worklist.Truncated: This list was cut short by this software, not by the server, so there are scheduled procedures it has not seen. Narrow the dates or the filters to be sure of a complete answer.
Worklist.Shortened: shortened to fit what DICOM allows
Worklist.Column.Name: Name
Settings.OrganizationUidRoot.ToolTip: Registered to the publisher of this software and fixed in it. It is shown partly masked and cannot be edited.
Settings.OrganizationUidRoot.Caption: Registered with Medical Connections Ltd and issued to the author of this software, so it is fixed and cannot be changed here. Choose it above when your PACS prefers identifiers under a registered arc; the UUID option is the default and is unique by construction.
Settings.StudyGrouping.Separate: Each file in its own study
Settings.StudyGrouping.ByPatient: Files for the same patient share one study
Settings.StudyGrouping.Caption: Grouping puts every file converted for the same Patient ID into one study, each file still in its own series, so a viewer shows them together but separately. The association lasts until the patient changes or the application is closed, and is never saved, so a later examination cannot join an old study by accident. A Study Instance UID typed on the form always wins.
Settings.ImageModality.Caption: Written to Modality (0008,0060) on converted images. OT (Other) is accepted everywhere. XC is the defined term for external camera photography. This is kept separate from the document modality because DOC would be wrong on a photograph.
Settings.RenderPdfPagesAsImages: Also send each page of a PDF as an image
Settings.RenderPdfPagesAsImages.Caption: Many PACS viewers will only open a study that contains an image, and an encapsulated PDF is not one. With this on, every page is also sent as a Secondary Capture image in its own series, so the viewer opens and the report is readable. Turn it off if your viewer already displays encapsulated documents; it roughly doubles what is stored and sent.
ConversionType.WSD: Workstation (created on a workstation or console)
ConversionType.SD: Scanned Document (a paper document scanned into DICOM)
ConversionType.DV: Digitized Video (captured from a video feed)
ConversionType.DI: Digital Interface (transferred via a digital interface)
ConversionType.DF: Digitized Film (an analog film X-ray or similar scanned via a digitizer)
ConversionType.SYN: Synthetic Image (an image created algorithmically or rendered from data)
Settings.BurnedInAnnotation: Document contains identifying text (Burned In Annotation)
Settings.AutoDelete: Delete the generated DICOM file after a successful transmission
Settings.AlwaysSaveLocally: Always keep a copy of the generated DICOM file
Settings.EnableFolderMonitoring: Monitor a folder for new PDF documents
Settings.ShowAdvancedFields: Show advanced DICOM fields on the main window

About.Offline: This application works entirely offline. The only network activity is the DICOM transmission to the configured destinations.
Settings.Import.Intro: Where documents arrive from another system with the patient details already in the file name, those details can be read instead of retyped. Nothing is sent without confirmation: the file name fills the form, and the operator still sees what is about to go and against whom.
Settings.Import.Enabled: Read the patient details from the file name
Settings.Import.Enabled.Caption: Applies to documents picked up from the monitored folder, which is configured on the Folders page. A file the operator opens by hand is never interpreted or moved.
Settings.Import.Patterns.Caption: Write the layout the way the names look, for example {PatientId}_{Name}_{AccessionNumber}. Available fields: {PatientId} {Name} {FamilyName} {GivenName} {AccessionNumber} {DateOfBirth} {StudyDescription}, and {*} for a part to ignore. Everything outside the braces must appear exactly as written. List as many layouts as you need; the one that reads the most fields is used, so the order does not matter. A line starting with regex: is a regular expression with named groups. Leave the extension out.
Settings.Import.DateFormats: Date of birth formats, one per line
Settings.Import.DateFormats.Caption: Leave empty to accept yyyyMMdd, yyyy-MM-dd, ddMMyyyy, dd-MM-yyyy and dd.MM.yyyy. A format containing a slash can never match, because a file name cannot contain one. A date that matches no format is left empty rather than guessed at, and the reason is written to the log.
Settings.Import.PadPatientId: Pad the patient number to this many digits
Settings.Import.PadPatientId.Caption: Sending systems often drop the leading zeros, writing 77 where your records hold 0000000077. Those are different patients as far as an archive is concerned. Set this to the width your archive stores, or 0 to use the number exactly as the file name has it. Only a number is padded: an identifier containing letters is left alone, and a longer one is never shortened.
Settings.Import.DefaultSex.Caption: File names almost never carry the sex. O means other, M and F are the obvious ones, and an empty box records the field as empty, which is also correct. The operator can change it on the form before sending.
Settings.Import.UseFileDate: Use the file's date as the study date
Settings.Import.UseFileDate.Caption: The date and time the file was created, which is normally when the other system issued the document. The date this application created the DICOM object is recorded separately, so both are kept. Switch this off to use the moment of conversion for both.
Settings.Import.SplitNames: Split a run-together name such as JohnDoe
Settings.Import.SplitNames.Caption: Reads JohnDoe as John Doe. This is a guess, and it is wrong for a surname such as McDonald or DaSilva, so it is off unless you know the sending software writes names this way. With it off, JohnDoe becomes the surname on its own. Try a real name in the box below before relying on it.
Settings.Import.After: Once a document has been dealt with
Settings.Import.After.Leave: Leave it alone (it will be offered again)
Settings.Import.After.Caption: The original must stop looking like new work, or the same document is offered every time. Nothing is ever deleted and nothing is ever overwritten: if a file of the same name is already there, a number is added to the new one.
Settings.Import.ImportedSubfolder: Subfolder for documents that were sent
Settings.Import.FailedSubfolder: Subfolder for documents that were not
Settings.Import.FailedSubfolder.Caption: A document that failed, or whose name matched no layout, always goes here, whatever the setting above says. It needs somebody to look at it, which cannot happen if it stays in the watched folder.
Settings.Import.RenameSuffix.Caption: Added after the extension, so report.pdf becomes report.pdf.imported and no longer looks like a PDF.
Settings.Import.Test.Caption: Type a real file name and see exactly what would be read from it. This uses the settings as they are above, so there is no need to save first. Nothing is converted and nothing is sent; the file does not even have to exist.
Settings.Import.Test.Empty: Type a file name above, then press Read it.
Settings.Lock.LockedCaption.Worklist: The worklist can be searched without a password. Changing which servers it talks to needs one, so a connection that works is not altered by accident. The same password opens the Destinations page.
Settings.Lock.LockedCaption.Destinations: Documents can be sent without a password. Changing where they are sent needs one: a mistyped address or AE Title puts a patient's report in the wrong archive. The same password opens the Worklist page.
Settings.Lock.Unprotected: No password has been set in this build, so these settings are open to anyone who opens this dialog. Run "pdftodicom settings-password" and rebuild to set one.
Settings.Worklist.Name: Name shown to the operator
Settings.Worklist.Name.Caption: What this worklist is called when the operator chooses between them, for example "Radiology" or "Cardiology". Say what the worklist holds rather than where it lives.
Worklist.NoServers: No worklist server is enabled. Add one on the Worklist page in Settings.
Worklist.PatientIdHint: Both boxes match on part of what you type and ignore capitals and accents, so goncalves finds Gonçalves. A single match is selected for you when the number you typed is the whole number; otherwise pick the right one from the list. Leave both boxes empty for the whole scheduled list. The name filed with the document is always the worklist's own spelling.
Worklist.DateRangeHint: This search covers these dates. It changes nothing for tomorrow: the dates this workstation uses by default are in Settings. A patient ID search ignores the dates entirely and looks at the whole worklist, so an older examination can be found by number; the Scheduled column shows which date each one belongs to.
Worklist.PageSummary: Page {0} of {1}, showing {2} to {3} of {4} found
Worklist.PageHint: The whole result is kept, not just this page. Use the page buttons to read the rest, or narrow the search to make it shorter.
Status.ConfigurationProblem: The settings could not be read
Settings.Import.Build: Build a layout by picking fields
Settings.Import.Build.Caption: Read a real file name from left to right and press the fields off in that order. Each one is added to the box below, separated by the character on the right. Press Add to put the finished layout in the list. You can also type or edit a layout by hand in the box underneath, which is where anything the buttons cannot express goes.
Settings.Import.Field.Name: Name
Settings.Lock.LockedCaption.Backup: This page writes and reads a file holding the addresses of the archives and worklist servers, and can replace the ones configured here. It needs the same password as the Destinations and Worklist pages.
Settings.Backup.Intro: Configure one workstation, export its connection settings, and import the file on the others. Only the archives and the worklist servers travel: this workstation's own AE Title, folders, language and templates stay as they are, because they are local to the machine.
Settings.Backup.IncludeDestinations: The archives documents are sent to
Settings.Backup.ExportCaption: Writes the entries as they appear on the other pages now, including anything just added.
Settings.Backup.ImportCaption: Nothing is written to this workstation until you press Save, so an import can still be abandoned with Cancel.
Settings.Backup.Mode: What an import does with the entries already here
Settings.Backup.Mode.Add: Add what is missing and keep the rest
Settings.Backup.Mode.Replace: Replace them with the file's entries
Settings.Backup.Exported: Exported {0} archive(s) and {1} worklist server(s) to {2}.
Settings.Backup.ExportFailed: The file could not be written: {0}
Settings.Backup.Imported: Imported {0} archive(s) and {1} worklist server(s). {2} were already configured here and were left alone, and {3} were discarded. Press Save to keep this.
Settings.Backup.ImportedNothing: Nothing changed: all {0} server(s) in the file are already configured here.
Settings.Backup.ConfirmReplace:
Replace will discard {0} archive(s) and {1} worklist server(s) configured on this workstation, and take the file's entries instead.

Nothing is written until you press Save.

Continue?
Settings.Backup.NothingChosenInFile: The file does not hold the kind of settings you asked to import. Tick what the file actually contains, or export it again including them.
Action.Exit.Tooltip: Close the application. Anything in progress is stopped, and you are asked first.
Exit.Confirm:
Close PDF to DICOM?

Anything typed into the form that has not been sent will be lost.
Exit.ConfirmBusy:
A conversion is still in progress.

Closing now stops it. If a document was part way through being sent, the archive may not have accepted it; nothing is deleted, so it can be sent again from the output folder.

Close anyway?
Settings.Lock.LockedCaption.Hl7: This page shows a patient's details and a destination's configuration together, which is the same material the Destinations and Worklist pages hold. It needs the same password.
Settings.Hl7.Title: Inspect a message
Settings.Hl7.Caption: Paste a message and the profile it should follow, and see what it carries, what is missing from it, and anything a receiver would object to. Nothing is sent from this page.
Settings.Hl7.DoesNotConform: The message does not satisfy this profile: {0} objection(s).
Settings.Hl7.ProfileNotUsable: The profile itself cannot be used, so the message was not checked against it.
Settings.Hl7.NotAMessage: That text could not be read as an HL7 message.
Settings.Hl7.Destinations.Title: Where messages are sent
Settings.Hl7.Destinations.Caption: One entry per receiving system. The four names are what the receiver reads from the message header, and the commonest reason a first message is rejected is one of them being wrong.
Settings.Hl7.TestCaption: Opens a connection and closes it. Nothing is sent, because a test message from this page would put a document in a patient's record to answer the question of whether a port is open.
Settings.Hl7.RetriesCaption: Leave this at zero unless the receiving system has confirmed it ignores a message it has already seen. A second attempt after a timeout can put a second copy of the document in the record.
Settings.Hl7.RestrictProfilesCaption: Leave this empty to accept any profile. A list restricts this destination, and a rule that sends it something else is reported rather than quietly skipped.
Settings.Hl7.Routing.Title: Which messages go where
Settings.Hl7.Routing.Caption: Rules are considered in order and the first rule to name a destination wins it, so a rule that matches everything belongs last. A message no rule matches is not sent.
Settings.Hl7.Announce: Announce a conversion to these systems
Settings.Hl7.AnnounceCaption: Off until an interface has been commissioned. While it is off, destinations and rules can be configured and tested and nothing is sent.
Settings.Hl7.Sequence.DicomThenHl7: Announce only what the archive accepted
Settings.Hl7.Sequence.Hl7ThenDicom: Announce first, and convert only if the message landed
Settings.Hl7.SequenceCaption: Independent is the careful answer: a record system that is down cannot stop a report reaching the archive. The third order is the only one in which an HL7 failure cancels a conversion.
Settings.Hl7.NothingConfigured: Nothing is configured here, so nothing is sent.
Settings.Hl7.CannotSaveLive: Announcements are switched on and the configuration cannot send anything. Correct the following, or switch announcements off while it is being worked on.
Settings.Hl7.RuleStopOnMatch: Stop considering rules once this one matches
Settings.Hl7.ConditionsCaption: All of them must hold. An empty list matches every message. A value of * matches anything that is present, and alternatives are separated by commas.
Settings.Hl7.Profiles.Title: Installed profiles
Settings.Hl7.Profiles.Caption: A profile is the message, its fields and where each value comes from, written against the receiving system's conformance statement. Import the file; it is copied here and kept.
Settings.Hl7.ProfileReplace: A profile called '{0}' is already installed. Replace it?
Settings.Hl7.ProfileRemoveConfirm: Remove the profile '{0}'? Any rule that uses it will stop working.
Settings.Hl7.Steps.Title: Setting one up, in order
Settings.Hl7.Steps.Body: 1. Profiles: install the example, or import the profile written from the receiving system's conformance statement.   2. Destinations: add the receiving system, then Test the connection.   3. Routing: add a rule saying which reports go there.   4. Routing: turn the switch on, once a test message has arrived.
Settings.Hl7.Steps.Example: New to this? The three Example buttons produce a working configuration that sends to a test receiver on this computer and reaches nothing real. Use them to see what belongs in each field, then change the destination to the hospital's own.
Settings.Hl7.Destinations.Required: Required. One entry per receiving system.
Settings.Hl7.Destinations.Example: For example: ris.hospital.local, port 2575, sending PDFTODICOM and RADIOLOGY, receiving RIS and HOSPITAL. The receiving system's administrator gives you all six.
Settings.Hl7.ExampleDestinationAdded: An example destination was added, pointing at {0} port {1}, which is this computer. Nothing real can be reached from it.
Settings.Hl7.Routing.Required: Required. At least one rule, and the switch below it.
Settings.Hl7.Routing.Example: For example: a rule called "Reports to the RIS", matching messageType = ORU, using the installed profile, sending to the destination you configured.
Settings.Hl7.Profiles.Required: Required. One profile, which decides what the message contains.
Settings.Hl7.Profiles.Example: The example is a complete ORU^R01 that announces a report and carries the Study Instance UID. Most receiving systems want something close to it, so it is a better starting point than an empty file.
Settings.Hl7.Inspector.Optional: Not required. Open this when a receiving system has rejected a message and you want to see what it was sent.
Settings.Hl7.SendTestMessageCaption: Builds a real message from invented values and sends it. This is the only check that proves the receiving system understands what this application produces. The patient is called ZZZTEST so that anybody who finds it knows it is a test.
Settings.Hl7.TestMessageConfirm:
A test message is about to be sent to '{0}' at {1}:{2}, using profile '{3}'.

This is a real message. If that address is a live record system, somebody there will see a patient called {4}.

Send it?
Settings.Hl7.TestNeedsProfile: No profile is installed, or none is selected for this destination, so no message can be built. Install one on the Profiles page first.
Confirm.Announcing: These record systems will be told about this document
Status.Hl7NeedsAttention: The document was handled. A message to a record system needs looking at.
